doc.title: Epic 3 Prep - Technical Specification
doc.snippet: UAT framework definition addressing Epic 2 retrospective finding: "No UAT framework despite working MCP tool". Defines 4-phase workflow (Readiness, Script Creation, Execution, Review) with pass/fail criteria (≥80% PASS, 60-79% PARTIAL, <60% FAIL). Templates enable repeatable user acceptance testing across all epics.

doc.title: RAGLite - Epic and Story Breakdown
doc.snippet: Epic goal: Enable multi-step reasoning and complex analytical workflows through agentic orchestration. Prep Sprint (Stories 3.0.1-3.0.5) addresses technical debt before feature implementation. UAT framework (Story 3.0.4) ensures usability validation before marking epics complete.

doc.title: Epic 2 Retrospective - Advanced RAG Architecture Enhancement
doc.section: Action Item 3: User Acceptance Testing (UAT) Framework
doc.snippet: Root cause: MCP server working since Epic 1 but no user-facing documentation or UAT process. Ricardo (Project Lead) unaware tool existed. Impact: Features built but not validated with real users. Decision: Create UAT framework for all epics with Ricardo as tester going forward.

doc.title: Testing Strategy
doc.snippet: E2E Tests (5% - Accuracy validation), Integration Tests (15% - Service integration), Unit Tests (80% - Code coverage). UAT complements automated testing by validating user-facing features manually. Testing standards define manual testing approach for documentation and user acceptance validation.

doc.title: RAGLite Coding Standards
doc.snippet: Documentation follows PEP 8 principles with specific requirements for markdown: Clear hierarchical structure (H1 for title, H2 for sections), code blocks with language tags (```markdown, ```bash), proper cross-references to other documentation. Templates should follow these formatting guidelines for consistency.

doc.title: Story 3.0.3: Document MCP Setup Guide
doc.snippet: Created comprehensive MCP setup guide (docs/setup/mcp-configuration.md, 258 lines) enabling Ricardo to connect Claude Desktop to RAGLite. KISS principle maintained (no custom scripts, direct JSON editing). Advisory notes: GitHub URL placeholder (LOW priority), screenshots for Settings>MCP (future enhancement). MCP guide enables UAT execution (Story 3.0.5).

constraint.details: Standard markdown templates (no custom frameworks), simple text-based test scenarios (no complex tooling), manual UAT execution (appropriate for user-facing features). No abstractions or automation for MVP.

Clear hierarchical structure (H1 for title, H2 for sections), code blocks with language tags, placeholder format: {{variable_name}}, proper cross-references to other documentation. Templates follow coding-standards.md formatting guidelines.

Templates designed for Bob (SM), Murat (Test Architect), Ricardo (UAT Tester), and future QA testers. Assume familiarity with testing concepts but provide clear structure. User-centric language for non-technical stakeholders.
Epic marked "done" only after UAT PASS (≥80%). If UAT FAIL, epic status remains "in-progress". UAT findings inform next epic's story creation. UX issues documented as lessons learned.

UAT focuses on user-facing validation (manual acceptance testing), complementing automated testing (pytest). Test scenarios require clear action, clear expectation, measurable pass/fail criteria, real user workflow.

interfaces.note: Story creates documentation templates (markdown files). No REST endpoints, GraphQL schemas, or code interfaces. Templates provide human-readable structure for UAT workflows and scripts.

standards.approach: Templates reviewed by team (Bob + Murat + Winston). Usability validated by applying to Epic 2 UAT (Story 3.0.5 prerequisite). Template review ensures completeness (all required sections), clarity (placeholders are clear), and reusability (works for any epic).
